body.statement: Maximum directed indegree one versus two is a sharp worst-case computational frontier for pointwise numerical edge identification with feasible rational positive-definite covariance: \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_1\) has deterministic polynomial bit complexity with constructive certificates, whereas \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_2\) is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete. At directed indegree zero there is no directed-edge query.
body.justification: The paired directions convert two isolated algorithmic facts into an exact structural boundary.
body.gap: No closest paper states a bounded-directed-fan-in frontier for numerical fibers; existing low-fan-in results are generic and existing numerical hardness is unrestricted.
body.consumer: Graphical SEM software can use the maximum directed indegree as a certified dispatch rule between exact specialized auditing and general real-algebraic methods.
